correctness.rationale: For unpadded binary-digit cumulative deficit a(n), Baruchel's exact Takagi identity and the Takagi quarter-map identities convert each shell minimum into a finite dyadic-grid maximum. The global Takagi bound 2/3 and the grid witness τ(3/8)=5/8 rule out outer quarters for depths >=3. Prefixing 01 and 10 bijects all maximizing words with those two levels below; H_1=1,H_2=2,H_l=2^(l−1)+H_(l−2)=floor(2^(l+1)/3). The first-half transfer j=n−2^k+1 has value 2^k−1−H_(k−1), while the second half is strictly worse. The parity-dependent maximizing word grammar follows inductively, and k=1 is checked directly. Independent exact digit sum enumeration verified full minimizing sets for shells k=1..14, including k=5 indices 36,37,38,40,41,42. Finite checks do not replace the induction.
residual_risks: Unpadded binary convention and half-open shells are essential; this is not a result about maxima or the full value distribution.
